column.name: calibration_type
column.description: SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::CALIBRATION_TYPE_* — relevance_score (samples real per-product text-relevance scores) or specificity (samples one per-query raw specificity value, no catalog query).

column.name: relevant_product_count
column.description: X: number of top-ranked products per search term assumed relevant, e.g. 6. Ignored (always 1 result per term) for calibration_type=specificity.

column.name: store_name
column.description: Store the calibration query runs against, e.g. DE — picked by the admin at upload time, since Zed has no implicit current store.

column.name: locale_name
column.description: Locale the calibration query runs against, e.g. de_DE — picked by the admin at upload time.

column.name: status
column.description: uploaded, skipped, calculating, calculated or failed.

column.name: computed_k
column.description: Pooled mean sampled value across all search terms; the calculated relevanceSaturationPoint or specificitySaturationPoint suggestion, depending on calibration_type.

column.name: sample_count
column.description: Total number of pooled values the stats were computed from.

column.name: total_count
column.description: Search term count, set once at upload time — the denominator for the live progress counter shown while status=calculating.

column.name: processed_count
column.description: Search terms fired so far in the current/last run — incremented one at a time inside ScoreCalibrator::calculate()'s own per-term loop, the numerator for the live progress counter.

column.name: products_found
column.description: Null until calculated; may be less than the run's relevant_product_count. Always 1 (or 0 on failure) for calibration_type=specificity.

column.name: values
column.description: Comma-separated raw sampled values — one per found product for calibration_type=relevance_score, exactly one raw specificity value for calibration_type=specificity. Null until calculated.

column.name: search_term
column.description: Canonical form: trimmed, lowercased, whitespace-collapsed — deliberately NOT tokenized, since real tokenization risks silently merging queries that are actually different asks.

column.name: importance_weight
column.description: Query Curator-editable, gated by standard Zed ACL. Flat default of 1 for every query until a human assigns real importance — see README.

column.name: customer_reference
column.description: A unique reference for a customer — same convention as spy_product_review.customer_reference, deliberately not a real foreign key to spy_customer (loose coupling across the Client/Zed boundary, standard Spryker pattern).

column.name: rating_type
column.description: heart, check, or x — see SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::RATING_TYPE_*.

column.name: metric_score
column.description: Query-importance-weighted nDCG aggregate across every rated query for this store/locale at this point in time (NOT rank_eval's own top-level metric_score, which is a plain unweighted mean — see RankEvaluationRunner).

column.name: query_count
column.description: How many rated queries actually contributed to this run.

column.name: source
column.description: SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::CHECKPOINT_SOURCE_* — 'manual' for now, later phases add further producers.

column.name: store_name
column.description: Which store this checkpoint's values were read from/apply to — search-ranking's config is store+locale scoped.

column.name: relevance_weight
column.description: search-ranking's relevanceWeight blend at the moment this checkpoint was taken.

column.name: specificity_blend_weight
column.description: search-ranking's specificityBlendWeight at the moment this checkpoint was taken (meaningful only if specificity weighting is enabled at the code level, but always captured — cheap and keeps a checkpoint a complete snapshot regardless of that project-level flag).

column.name: specificity_curve_exponent
column.description: search-ranking's specificityCurveExponent at the moment this checkpoint was taken. Defaults 1.0 (the Hill-equation identity value) so migrating an existing table backfills every pre-existing checkpoint row with the value that reproduces its own original curve exactly, not an arbitrary placeholder.

column.name: specificity_weight_exponent
column.description: search-ranking's specificityWeightExponent at the moment this checkpoint was taken.

column.name: specificity_weight_shift_magnitude
column.description: search-ranking's specificityWeightShiftMagnitude at the moment this checkpoint was taken.

column.name: is_specificity_weighting_enabled
column.description: Whether search-ranking's code-level specificity-weighting flag was on at the moment this checkpoint was taken — independent of the 4 knob values above, so a checkpoint honestly records whether those numbers were actually live, not just what they were set to.

column.name: metric_weights
column.description: JSON array of {idSearchRankingMetric, name, weight} — every metric's own weight at the moment this checkpoint was taken, active or not.

column.name: fk_search_ranking_metric
column.description: Soft reference to search-ranking's own metric id — no hard foreign key, same discipline as spy_search_ranking_weight_checkpoint.metric_weights: the metric could be deleted between config edits and a later run, handled as a safe skip.

column.name: store_name
column.description: e.g. DE — what auto-tune is checking (a metric's formula/shape) lives on search-ranking's own spy_search_ranking_metric_store_config, which is store+locale scoped since that package's isLocaleScoped unification; this table matches that grain now, same as store_name+locale_name below. Auto-Tune used to operate on a single hardcoded store regardless of how many real stores existed; this column is what makes every configured store get its own independent monthly check.

column.name: locale_name
column.description: e.g. de_DE. Saving via AutoTuneMetricConfigWriterInterface fans the SAME threshold/auto-update/notify settings out to every real locale of the store when the metric is search-ranking's own isLocaleScoped=false (the common case, matching how formula/weight already fan out there) — one row per locale unconditionally, but usually all identical. For an isLocaleScoped=true metric, each locale is saved and read fully independently; a locale never explicitly configured has no row here and is simply skipped by the monthly run, same 'absence means opted out' contract auto_tune_threshold itself already has.

column.name: auto_tune_threshold
column.description: R² floor below which the metric is flagged as needing attention. NULL opts the metric out of auto-tune entirely — the default for every metric until an admin explicitly sets one.

column.name: is_auto_update_enabled
column.description: Whether crossing the threshold triggers an automatic refit, or only a proposal/notification.

column.name: auto_update_scope
column.description: SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::AUTO_UPDATE_SCOPE_* — only consulted when is_auto_update_enabled is true.

column.name: is_notify_enabled
column.description: Whether crossing the threshold sends the before/after summary email, independently of is_auto_update_enabled.

column.name: algorithm
column.description: SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::OPTIMIZATION_ALGORITHM_* — which algorithm this run uses.

column.name: is_termination_criteria_trusted
column.description: Whether this run calls the algorithm's own trustTerminationCriteria(), governing the run by its convergence/divergence/plateau detection instead of the fixed maxGenerations budget. False (the default) preserves the original fixed-budget behavior.

column.name: warm_start_fraction
column.description: How much of the search is seeded from the live configuration instead of starting cold, passed to the algorithm's own setWarmStart(). 0.0 (the default) preserves the original from-scratch behavior; 1.0 fully seeds from the live configuration.

column.name: fixed_relevance_weight
column.description: A human's own choice at queue time to pin relevanceWeight at exactly this value instead of searching it — null (the default) preserves the original always-free behavior.

column.name: fixed_specificity_curve_exponent
column.description: Same pin choice as fixed_relevance_weight, for specificityCurveExponent. Meaningless (ignored) when specificity weighting is disabled at the code level.

column.name: fixed_specificity_weight_exponent
column.description: Same pin choice as fixed_relevance_weight, for specificityWeightExponent.

column.name: fixed_specificity_weight_shift_magnitude
column.description: Same pin choice as fixed_relevance_weight, for specificityWeightShiftMagnitude.

column.name: fixed_specificity_blend_weight
column.description: Same pin choice as fixed_relevance_weight, for specificityBlendWeight.

column.name: fixed_metric_weights
column.description: JSON array of {name, weight} — metrics a human chose to pin at queue time, same encoding as best_metric_weights. Null/empty means none were pinned by hand (a metric can still end up held constant anyway if its own formula is non-deterministic — that's decided at run time, never persisted here).

column.name: status
column.description: SearchRankingOptimizerConfig::OPTIMIZATION_RUN_STATUS_* — queued, running, done or failed.

column.name: total_count
column.description: Total planned candidate evaluations (population size * generations), set once the run actually starts — the denominator for the live progress counter shown while status=running. Once is_termination_criteria_trusted is true, this is the algorithm's own safety-ceiling estimate, not a realistic prediction — a converged run stops well short of it.

column.name: processed_count
column.description: Candidate evaluations completed so far in the current/last run — the numerator for the live progress counter.

column.name: generations_used
column.description: The real number of generations the algorithm actually ran (count of OptimizationResult::getBestValueHistory()), set once status=done. Independent of total_count/processed_count, which count candidate evaluations, not generations -- this is what actually answers whether early termination fired and how much of the budget a run really needed.

column.name: baseline_score
column.description: The live configuration's own weighted nDCG score at the moment this run started, for comparison against the winning candidate — null until the run starts.

column.name: best_relevance_weight
column.description: The winning candidate's relevanceWeight. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_metric_weights
column.description: JSON array of {idSearchRankingMetric, name, weight} for the winning candidate — same shape/encoding as spy_search_ranking_weight_checkpoint.metric_weights. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_score
column.description: The winning candidate's own weighted nDCG score. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_specificity_blend_weight
column.description: The winning candidate's specificityBlendWeight. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_specificity_curve_exponent
column.description: The winning candidate's specificityCurveExponent. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_specificity_weight_exponent
column.description: The winning candidate's specificityWeightExponent. Null until status=done.

column.name: best_specificity_weight_shift_magnitude
column.description: The winning candidate's specificityWeightShiftMagnitude. Null until status=done.

column.name: applied_at
column.description: When a human clicked Apply on this run's winning candidate — writing it through search-ranking's own facade and republishing. Null means either not done yet, or done but never applied. Always propose-only: nothing here is ever set automatically.
